summary: Barbara E. Ward was a sinologist who studied at Newnham College, the University of London, and the London School of Economics. She held posts at the University of London, Cambridge, Cornell, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She has held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Vienna.

Barbara Harriss-White works in Indology and development studies. Educated at Newstead Wood School, she held academic posts at the University of East Anglia (~1979–1990), Queen Elizabeth House (~1990–2011), and the University of Oxford (~1990).

Barbara Mittler is a sinologist and historian. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she also held a post in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran.

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Stella Kramrisch, and Royal W. Weiler. She taught at Barnard College and Columbia University.

Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under G. Raj. She has been affiliated with Mount Allison University.
Barend Faddegon was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Amsterdam from around 1893 to 1906 and later served as an emeritus professor there from 1907 to 1944.

Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and held academic positions at Heidelberg University, Leiden University, and the University of Hamburg.

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University, holding posts at ANU, the University of Munich, the University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, the University of Southern California, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington, CIHTS, and the University of Hong Kong.
Bart Dessein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and serves as an associate professor at Ghent University.

Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian who studied at Kiel University. He held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1810 to 1813 and at the University of Bonn from around 1823 to 1831.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He was a professor of Greek at the University of Virginia and later taught at Johns Hopkins University.

Batakrishna Ghosh was an Indologist and linguist who completed doctoral studies under Hanns Oertel between 1933 and 1935. He served as a librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and edited the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902. He headed the Buryat Scientific Center and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Beata Grant is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and a faculty post at Washington University in St. Louis.

Beatrice Erskine Lane was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Radcliffe College and Columbia University under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana. In 1921, she held a professorship at Otani University.

Beatrix Pfleiderer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, Heidelberg University, the University of Hamburg, Viadrina, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Vienna (~1905–1919) and Charles University (~1919–1952).
